summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with abdominal fullness, right upper quadrant pain, black stools, and confusion in the setting of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis. He had a history of hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Initial evaluation revealed moderate ascites and stable lab values, with no active bleeding or infection. He experienced episodes of hepatic encephalopathy during the stay, which resolved with continuation of lactulose and rifaximin. A low dose of escitalopram was started for depressive symptoms. He had one episode of non-bloody vomiting on the day of planned discharge but remained stable. By discharge, his mental status had cleared, pain was improved, and he was able to eat. He was discharged home on all prior medications plus escitalopram, with follow-up planned in transplant, hepatology, and primary care clinics.
problems: Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Unspecified viral hepatitis C with hepatic coma
Nonspecific abnormal findings in stool contents
